output: This review looked at how well Portable Occult Trauma Scanners (POCS) work in detecting injuries after accidents. It found that POCS is quite good at spotting injuries, especially in adults and mixed populations. For children, it's less accurate. POCS helps doctors decide if someone might have injuries, but it can't always tell if there are no injuries. For chest injuries, it works well, but for abdominal injuries, it often misses them. So, when POCS says someone has an injury, it's usually right, but when it says someone doesn't have an injury, it might be wrong. Doctors should use other tests like CT scans to check for abdominal injuries if POCS says there might be none. More studies are needed to confirm if POCS is better at spotting chest injuries.
